brief.outcome: Get Android crash-free users (Firebase Crashlytics) back above 99.3% and the Play Store rating back to 4.2 within two months, by finding and fixing the crashes behind the checkout complaints and shipping the fixes through staged rollout with the mobile lead's approval.

ambition.goal_beyond: Checkout on Android stays reliable, so ratings recover and a bad release is caught in its first rollout step instead of in the reviews.
rungs: Fix the top crashes at checkout and ship the fix
Find which release, devices and code paths cause the crashes, fix the biggest clusters through staged rollout, and read the result against Google's own Android vitals as well as Crashlytics
Keep it true without being asked: a release gate and a standing crash watch that flag a regression in the first rollout step
ambition.judge: Android vitals user-perceived crash rate and rating by app version, read directly in Play Console (Google's own count of users, separate from Crashlytics), before and after, over the same number of days

brief.deliverable: Draft pull requests that fix the top Android crashes (each with a regression test), a staged rollout plan with halt rules, the fixes released step by step with the mobile lead's approval, and a results readout against Crashlytics and Android vitals.

research.approach: Practitioners start from the raw crash data, not the headline percentage. They check that Crashlytics and Google's Android vitals agree (they count differently: users versus sessions), line up the start of the drop with a release, then group crashes into issues, read symbolicated stack traces and reproduce the biggest clusters with the right device, OS and memory conditions. Fixes are small, carry a regression test, and ship by staged rollout while the new version is compared with the old one on the same days; the rollout is halted, not widened, if the new version is worse. Ratings follow later, so the outcome is read against Android vitals as well as the star rating.

sources.title: Crashes in Android vitals (Android Developers)
sources.note: Official definitions of crash rate and user-perceived crash rate by daily active users; bad behavior thresholds of 1.09% overall and 8% per device model that reduce Play discoverability. Page shows no publish date; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Crashes: diagnose and fix (Android Developers)
sources.note: How to read a stack trace, reproduce memory and network crashes on an emulator, use logcat, and why null pointer exceptions are the largest cause of crashes on Google Play. Page shows no publish date; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Release an app update with a staged rollout (Play Console Help)
sources.note: A staged rollout does not widen by itself; you raise the percentage, halt it (no new users get the version) or resume it. Advises watching crash reports and feedback closely. Page shows only a 2026 copyright; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Crashlytics troubleshooting and FAQ (Firebase)
sources.note: Crash-free users needs the latest SDK, automatic reporting on and Analytics; opt-in reporting makes it less reliable. Regressed issues reopen only for versions that had not reported before. ANR counts differ from Android vitals. Page shows no publish date; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Configure and receive Crashlytics alerts (Firebase)
sources.note: Regressed and trending alerts are on by default; new-issue and velocity alerts stay off until a channel is chosen. Velocity default is 1% of sessions and 25 users. Page shows no publish date; accessed 2026-11-03.

steps.name: Pull raw crash events and Android vitals by version, device and day
steps.why: The headline 97.1% hides which release, devices and screens carry the crashes; the grouped issue list and the vitals series show it.

steps.name: Check the crash numbers can be trusted
steps.why: Crashlytics counts sessions and Android vitals counts users, crash-free users needs Analytics and automatic reporting, and unreadable stack traces stall diagnosis.

steps.name: Line up the review complaints with crash timing and app version
steps.why: Confirms the rating drop is crash-driven and shows which flow users say breaks.

steps.name: Group crashes by cause, read the stack traces and reproduce the biggest clusters
steps.why: Stack trace exception type and frame point to the cause; device, OS and memory conditions are needed to reproduce.

steps.name: Rank fixes by users affected, effort and risk, and let the mobile lead choose
steps.why: A few clusters usually carry most crashed users; the lead owns the release risk.

steps.name: Make the smallest fix for each chosen cause, with a regression test, as a draft pull request
steps.why: A test that fails on the old code proves the fix and stops a repeat.

steps.name: Plan and run the staged rollout with halt rules
steps.why: A staged rollout only widens when someone raises it and can be halted; watching the new version against the old one limits the damage of a bad fix.

steps.name: Read the result against Android vitals, Crashlytics and the rating
steps.why: Two independent counts of crashes plus the rating by version show whether the fix worked rather than the season.

steps.name: Reply to low-star reviews
steps.why: Replies can win back some ratings once the fix is live.

steps.name: Check whether iOS has the same checkout problem
steps.why: A shared backend or API cause would show up on both platforms.

steps.name: Save what was learned and propose a release gate and crash watch
steps.why: Keeps the result true: regressions are caught in the first rollout step.

pitfalls.text: Comparing Crashlytics crash-free users with Android vitals as if they were the same number: one counts sessions, the other users.
Reading crash-free users when automatic reporting or Analytics is off or reporting is opt-in; the figure is then unreliable.
Closing an issue instead of muting it, so a later version reopens it as a regression, or assuming it is fixed when it reappears on a new version.
Fixing the loudest stack trace without checking it is the checkout path or that it reproduces on the affected devices and Android versions.
Widening a staged rollout on a hope: the percentage never rises by itself and users who got a bad version stay on it after a halt.
Expecting the star rating to move at once; it follows the fix, so judge the fix by crash rate first.

stages.name: Pin down the problem
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured problem, target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Gather the raw crash data
stages.goal: Pull the crash issues and events and the Android vitals series for the last 8 weeks, with the release history, into one folder in this project.

checks.name: Crashlytics crash-free users for the latest 7 days matches the reported 97.1% within 0.3 points, or the difference is explained
Android vitals user-perceived crash rate is recorded next to Crashlytics for the same days; if not available, marked unknown
Every app version live in the period has crash-free users and a release date

stages.name: Read the review complaints
stages.goal: Take the last 8 weeks of Play reviews with their app version and sort the 1 to 3 star ones into themes, with counts and quotes.

outputs.name: Review themes by week and version

checks.name: The number of reviews read matches the Play Console total for the same dates within 2%
Every theme shows its count, share of low-star reviews and two quotes with dates
Share of low-star reviews that mention crashing, freezing or closing, and the share that name checkout, is stated

stages.name: Check the crash numbers can be trusted
stages.goal: Check how crash-free users is counted, that reporting is on and stack traces are readable, and explain any gap between Crashlytics and Android vitals before anyone reasons from them.

checks.name: At least 9 of the top 10 issues show readable, deobfuscated frames; otherwise the mapping-file gap is listed as a fix
Automatic reporting, Analytics and SDK version are checked and recorded, because crash-free users depends on them
Gap between Crashlytics and Android vitals is explained (users versus sessions) or marked unresolved
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for diagnosis

stages.name: Find what is crashing checkout and why
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses against the evidence: group crashes into issues, read the stack traces against the code, line up the start with a release, and reproduce the biggest clusters on the devices and Android versions affected. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every listed hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the number or stack trace behind it
The issues diagnosed cover at least 70% of crashed Android users, or the uncovered share is stated
Each cause named for a top issue cites the stack frame and the file and line in the repository
Each top cause is reproduced (device or emulator settings stated) or marked NOT REPRODUCED with what is missing
Each main finding names a competing explanation

stages.name: Rank the fixes
stages.goal: Turn supported causes into ranked fix cards: share of crashed users each would remove, effort, risk and how it will be measured.

checks.name: Every card cites the diagnosis finding it rests on
Every card states the share of crashed Android users it would remove and the expected crash-free users gain, summing to no more than 100% of the gap
Cards are ranked by users removed per unit of effort, with measurement or mapping-file fixes first when the data check was LIMITED

stages.name: Mobile lead chooses
stages.goal: The mobile lead picks the fix cards and the rollout rules (step sizes and when to halt). Ask for the reason when a top card is passed over.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are recorded with the lead's reason wherever the top card was passed over
A numeric halt rule is set for the new version at each rollout step

stages.name: Draft the fixes
stages.goal: For each chosen cause, make the smallest fix and a regression test as a draft pull request, and check it before the mobile lead sees it.

outputs.name: Draft pull request list with notes

checks.name: Only chosen causes are touched; each diff lists the files and why each changed
Each regression test fails on the old code and passes on the fix, with the command and result shown, or is marked NOT RUN
A second reviewer finds no unresolved blocker in any pull request

stages.name: Plan the staged rollout
stages.goal: Write the go or no-go list, the rollout steps with halt rules from the decision, what to watch at each step and the recovery plan if the new version is worse.

checks.name: Go or no-go list has every line marked Pass, Fail or Not supplied
Each step names what to read (new version versus old version crash-free users and user-perceived crash rate on the same days), how long to wait, and the halt number
A recovery path is written for a worse new version, including that users who already have it stay on it after a halt

stages.name: Release step by step
stages.goal: With the mobile lead, move the approved build through each rollout step, reading Crashlytics and Android vitals for the new version against the old one before the next step.

checks.name: Each step has the mobile lead's approval recorded before it was raised
After each step the rollout percentage is read back from Play Console and matches what was approved
A step is halted, not widened, if the new version breaks the halt rule set at the decision

stages.name: Read the results honestly
stages.goal: Compare the new version with the old on the same days at each step, then read Android crash-free users, Android vitals and the rating against the target and guardrails.

checks.name: Fixed and unfixed versions are compared on the same days, not before versus after only
Verdict states both the Crashlytics figure and the Android vitals user-perceived crash rate
A verdict is given only when the new version has enough users for crash-free users to be read to 0.1 points; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
Rating, user-perceived crash rate against the 1.09% threshold and checkout completion are each checked
A missed target is reported with the numbers, and the rating is judged by version cohort given its lag

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close the work, write a blameless learning note on how the crashes shipped, and propose a release gate and a crash watch for the mobile lead to accept or reject.

checks.name: Timeline from first bad release to fix cites sources and dates
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this app, this business or the playbook, and who owns it
The crash-watch proposal gives a numeric alert threshold and where the alert goes, and nothing is switched on without the mobile lead's yes

hypotheses.test: Crash-free users by app version and by day since rollout, against the release and rollout dates.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The newest version(s) sit at least 1 point below the previous version on the same days since rollout, and the fall starts within 2 days of a rollout step.
hypotheses.refute_if: All versions fall together on the same calendar days, or no release lines up.

hypotheses.statement: A few issues on the checkout path cause most crashed users.
hypotheses.test: Rank issues by users; mark the ones whose stack trace, screen or breadcrumb is cart or checkout.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The top 5 issues cover 60% or more of crashed Android users and at least half of those are on the checkout path.
hypotheses.refute_if: Crashes are spread thinly with no issue above 10% of crashed users.

hypotheses.statement: The crashes are concentrated on certain devices or Android versions.
hypotheses.test: Crash-free users and Android vitals user-perceived crash rate by device model and Android version.
hypotheses.confirm_if: One device model or Android version has a crash rate at least twice the overall rate with enough users to read.
hypotheses.refute_if: Rates are within 25% of each other across the main devices and versions.

hypotheses.statement: A third-party library, payment SDK, WebView or Android platform change caused it, not our code.
hypotheses.test: Top frames in library packages; whether the rise began on a date with no release of ours.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Top issue frames are in a library package, or the rise began on a date with no release.
hypotheses.refute_if: Top frames are in our own checkout code and the rise follows our release.

hypotheses.statement: Part of the problem is memory or freezes, not exceptions.
hypotheses.test: Split events by exception type, and read the ANR rate in Android vitals.
hypotheses.confirm_if: OutOfMemoryError events or ANRs are 25% or more of crashed users, or the ANR rate is at or above Google's bad behavior threshold.
hypotheses.refute_if: Under 10% of crashed users and ANR rate below the threshold.

hypotheses.statement: Part of the Crashlytics drop is a measurement problem, not users crashing more.
hypotheses.test: Compare Crashlytics crash-free users with Android vitals for the same days; check reporting settings, SDK version and Analytics.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Android vitals user-perceived crash rate did not rise while Crashlytics fell by 2 points or more, or reporting settings changed in the window.
hypotheses.refute_if: Both counts moved together and settings were stable.

hypotheses.statement: The rating fell mostly because of crashes, not other causes.
hypotheses.test: Share of 1 to 3 star reviews since the drop that mention crashing, freezing or closing, by app version.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least half of new low-star reviews mention a crash, freeze or app closing.
hypotheses.refute_if: Fewer than a quarter do; then the rating needs other work and the 4.2 target is flagged.

measurement.window: At least 7 days at each rollout step, comparing the new version with the old one on the same days; then the 28 days after full rollout for the headline figures.
measurement.min_volume: Enough users on the new version at each step for crash-free users to be read to 0.1 points; the count is read from Crashlytics at each step and is not known today.
measurement.stop_rule: Halt a step and tell the mobile lead if the new version's crash-free users is below the old version's by the margin set at the decision, or Android vitals user-perceived crash rate for the new version rises above 1.09%.

dropped.reason: Outside the request and needs the owner's voice; revisit after the fix lands.
The request is Android; iOS is only looked at if the evidence shows the same cause.
